defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Editor or docs: the term comes from the editor itself or its official documentation.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a model run step by step from stated rules, not a measurement of a real game.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: It compiles is a claim, and a clean log proves only the bottom rung.
A headless run prints values, but only a person at a screen sees pixels.
A pinned clock and a fixed random seed make a run repeat.
Colour textures get the source color hint, and normal maps stay as data.
A loose tolerance gives false passes, and a tight one gives false fails.
A new test must fail on known-bad code and pass on known-good code.
bookends.command: Quiz me on shader verification terms with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms claim versus evidence, observed versus inferred, headless mode, bench scene, test fixture, golden image, tolerance, false positive, specification oracle and mutation check. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.
checks: Check: each case is about making a game, and the answer waits for you.
Check: you named the exact term and said why its look-alike does not fit.

beats.narration_text: A ladder of five rungs for a shader change. The Evidence ladder ranks kinds of proof, each rung proving something the rung below cannot. Parse, contract, driver and model can all be checked headless, with no window. Only the top rung, observation, needs a person at a screen. For example, an agent says the hit flash on your player sprite works. If it only loaded the shader without an error, that claim stands on the bottom rung.

Zero SHADER ERROR lines in the log is the evidence, and it proves rung one, parse, and nothing about rungs two to five. For example, a coding agent reports that the water shader in your level compiles. The evidence is the log of your own run, searched for SHADER ERROR, with a count of zero.

beats.narration_text: Two panels, what a windowless run can print, and what only the GPU, the graphics processor, draws. Headless mode is a run with no window, so no pixels are drawn. It still prints values and logic, such as the flash amount on every frame and seven bench checks. It cannot show the body or eye colour, or whether it looks right. For example, a headless test can confirm your player's flash value rises at a hit, but not that the sprite visibly flashed.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap. It compiles is a claim, and a clean log proves only the bottom rung. A headless run prints values, but only a person at a screen sees pixels. A pinned clock and a fixed random seed make a run repeat. Colour textures get the source color hint, and normal maps stay as data. A loose tolerance gives false passes, and a tight one gives false fails. A new test must fail on known-bad code and pass on known-good code.
